items.title: WILDCARD TIME? 🤔 | FPL CHAI'S GW6 TRANSFER PLANS! 🚨 | FPL Tips 26/27
items.headline: Brighton triple-up and Haaland shape the Gameweek 6 wildcard debate
items.summary:
Gameweek 6 is presented as a strong wildcard window, particularly for managers whose squads are weighed down by awkward fixtures and who still hold a Bench Boost for Gameweek 7. The three-week international break offers time to monitor injuries and chase price changes, although it also raises the risk of players returning unfit. A Gameweek 6 wildcard can be built to Bench Boost in Gameweek 7, with Fulham, Brighton, Arsenal and Manchester City assets offering attractive short-term fixtures.

Joao Pedro is the central decision. If fit, Chelsea’s forward is viewed as close to a season-long hold because of his link play, output and favourable price, while Chelsea’s attack looks notably weaker without him. However, uncertainty over his knee issue and international-break availability makes him risky for anyone planning a Gameweek 7 Bench Boost: an injured Pedro leaves a wildcard squad unable to maximise all 15 players. Alternatives such as Brighton’s Charalampos Kostoulas, Fulham’s Gonzalo, Brentford’s Igor Thiago, Leeds’ Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Newcastle’s Yoane Wissa are considered, with the debate largely coming down to fixtures, penalties and whether Pedro is confirmed fit.

Brighton assets demand attention despite a difficult-looking run that includes Liverpool and Manchester City. Their 3-0 win over Arsenal reinforces the view that Fabian Hurzeler’s side can score against any opponent. Pascal Gross is a leading midfield target after a goal and assist, while Diego Gomez remains an assist threat and Kostoulas is a cheap forward differential after his early returns. At the back, Luka Vuskovic combines a secure role, set-piece threat and DefCon potential. Brentford’s Kevin Schade is another standout midfielder: he is playing 90 minutes, has three goals and two assists, and Brentford’s settled structure makes him more appealing than the more volatile options around his price.

The proposed Bench Boost-focused wildcard contains David Raya and Bernd Leno; Riccardo Calafiori, Vuskovic, Antonee Robinson, Josko Gvardiol and Micky van de Ven; Gross, Schade, Bukayo Saka, Marcus Tavernier and Bryan Mbeumo; plus Erling Haaland, Pedro and Kostoulas. Raya and Calafiori provide Arsenal’s defensive security without committing to a triple-up, while Gvardiol benefits from Manchester City’s improved defensive numbers and flexibility between left-back and centre-back. Leno and Robinson target Fulham’s Ipswich, Hull and Coventry run, although doubling on their defence is mainly justified for a Gameweek 7 Bench Boost rather than as a long-term commitment. Tavernier is selected ahead of Bournemouth’s excellent Gameweek 9 fixture swing, and Mbeumo offers Manchester United attacking exposure against Tottenham and Leeds.

Haaland is an automatic inclusion, with Ipswich at home in Gameweek 7 also a potential Triple Captain opportunity. Liverpool assets are increasingly expendable after Bournemouth because of the upcoming Manchester City meeting, while Tottenham defenders and attackers are treated cautiously after another poor defensive display and blunt attacking performance. Arsenal defenders remain viable despite Brighton’s win, but their attack is less convincing as an FPL investment than their clean-sheet and DefCon routes at the back.
key_points: Gameweek 6 is a preferred wildcard point, especially for managers planning to Bench Boost in Gameweek 7 after the international break.
Erling Haaland is a non-negotiable wildcard pick, with Ipswich at home in Gameweek 7 a major captaincy and possible Triple Captain fixture.
Joao Pedro stays the best-value forward if fit, but his knee issue makes him a significant Bench Boost risk until his availability is confirmed.
Brighton’s Gross, Vuskovic and Kostoulas are key targets after their 3-0 win at Arsenal, even with Liverpool and Manchester City in their next four matches.
Kevin Schade is Brentford’s preferred attacking asset because he is playing 90 minutes and has three goals and two assists already.
Fulham’s Leno and Robinson are short-term Bench Boost enablers for Ipswich away, Hull at home and Coventry away, rather than essential long-term holds.
Manchester City’s Gvardiol is favoured for defensive solidity, attacking potential and his ability to retain minutes at centre-back if needed.
Liverpool assets are candidates to sell after Gameweek 5, while Tottenham assets remain difficult to trust after their defensive collapse and lack of attacking quality.

items.title: FPL GW6 TRANSFER PLANS ✅ MY GAMEWEEK 6 TEAM 🎯
items.headline: Palmer edges Saka and Haaland in a tight Gameweek 6 captaincy call
items.summary:
Gameweek 5 produces a red arrow from 44 points, but holding João Pedro proves valuable despite his injury absence against Brentford. Selling him would have required buying him back, while the Gross-over-Barry selection gains points after Pascal Groß delivers another huge return. João Pedro’s availability remains the key team-news issue for Gameweek 6, although Chelsea manager Enzo Maresca offers little reliable injury information and Chelsea look disjointed without him in the 3-0 defeat at Brentford.

Brentford assets merit attention despite upcoming trips to Aston Villa and Liverpool. Kevin Schade, at £6.1m, has three goals and two assists in five matches and looks secure for minutes, while Thiago gets on the scoresheet but picks up a booking. Chelsea’s attacking upside remains high, but owning two or three of their attackers carries major volatility: there are explosive weeks when combinations click, but blanks can be painful. Manchester United are viewed as an avoid, while Fulham’s run against Ipswich, Hull and Coventry makes Gonzalo Garcia, Josh King, Bernd Leno and Andersen-style defensive options attractive. King in particular is a £5.5m differential after an energetic display against United.

Arsenal’s 3-0 loss to Brighton is treated as an anomaly rather than a reason to abandon their defence. Double Arsenal defence plus Bukayo Saka remains a preferred long-term structure, although Gabriel is less compelling at his price when cheaper defenders such as Konsa can offer similar returns. Arsenal lead the clean-sheet projections over the next five Gameweeks, while Fulham, Everton and Manchester City also rate well. Leeds continue to post encouraging defensive numbers, making the £5.0m Muramović a potential set-and-forget target from Gameweek 8, with defensive contribution points and goal threat adding to his appeal.

The current Gameweek 6 squad starts Raya; Konsa, Chalobah and Digne; Saka, Cole Palmer, Szoboszlai and Groß; João Pedro, Erling Haaland and Wissa. If João Pedro is fit, the preferred move is to roll the transfer and reach four free transfers. If he remains out, Mendy can deputise against Everton, or Sangaré can become a £6m midfielder such as Tavernier or Schade. Josh King is also appealing as a like-for-like Sangaré replacement because it preserves the budget for a later Digne-to-Silva move and a route to Muramović. Captaincy is finely balanced between Saka at home to Leeds, Palmer at home to Bournemouth and Haaland away to Liverpool; Palmer currently gets the armband, with Haaland vice, but Haaland’s record against Liverpool keeps him firmly in contention.
key_points: Cole Palmer is the provisional Gameweek 6 captain against Bournemouth, with Saka versus Leeds and Haaland at Liverpool the other leading options.
Hold João Pedro if he is passed fit; if he starts, rolling the transfer to build four free transfers is the preferred plan.
Josh King is a strong £5.5m differential for Fulham’s Ipswich, Hull and Coventry run and can replace Sangaré without damaging future transfer plans.
Kevin Schade is a viable £6.1m midfield buy after three goals and two assists in five Gameweeks, despite difficult immediate fixtures.
Do not overreact to Arsenal’s 3-0 defeat at Brighton: double Arsenal defence remains a sound long-term strategy on clean-sheet projections.
Muramović is a leading Gameweek 8 defensive target at £5.0m as Leeds combine strong underlying defensive numbers with his attacking and defensive-contribution potential.
Silva is under consideration from Gameweek 7, starting with Sunderland at home, if Digne becomes a minutes risk.
Haaland remains difficult to sell despite his £15.6m price, as a balanced squad can still accommodate him alongside Saka and Palmer.

items.title: FPL Kneejerk Gameweek 6 🔥 BIG red arrow 📉 A rather Gross week 😭
items.headline: Sangare becomes the priority sale as Sharda and King emerge for Gameweek 6
items.summary:
A 38-point Gameweek 5 leaves the squad with three free transfers but no need for a rushed move during the three-week international break. The main regret is benching Pascal Gross for Sangare, although saving transfers softens the damage and keeps flexibility high. With Arsenal’s home meeting with Leeds, Chelsea’s home game against Bournemouth, Newcastle’s trip to Coventry and Manchester City’s trip to Liverpool all on the horizon, the current team remains viable for Gameweek 6 despite the poor score.

Sangare is the clearest issue. His failure to start, combined with his reliance on defensive-contribution points, makes reduced minutes especially damaging: unlike an attacking player, he has little chance of salvaging a return in a 60-minute appearance. Sharda is an appealing replacement despite Brentford facing Aston Villa away and Liverpool at home next; his longer-term run from Gameweek 8 is strong, and reliable 90-minute appearances would make him attractive. Josh King is another inexpensive midfield option, while Pascal Gross remains the preferred sub-£6m midfielder, even if his recent output is unsustainably high.

Dominik Szoboszlai is sellable but not an automatic priority over Sangare. His lack of open-play returns, possible penalty uncertainty and earlier substitution against Liverpool raise concerns, particularly if he is no longer a dependable 90-minute player. However, selling him simply because of frustration while retaining Sangare makes little sense when most appealing replacements cost £6.5m or less. If Joao Pedro is fit after the break, rolling a transfer to reach four in Gameweek 7 is a realistic option; if Pedro remains out, a switch to Gonzalo Garcia is under consideration, with Garcia viewed as a viable budget forward who may also have penalties.

Captaincy is unsettled. Cole Palmer currently holds the armband for Bournemouth at home, with Erling Haaland an alternative despite Liverpool away; Bruno Fernandes is also considered a strong captaincy candidate if a route to him opens. Bruno is a definite keep for those who own him rather than wildcarding, even amid Manchester United’s poor form. Bukayo Saka is also in the conversation for Leeds at home, while Palmer versus Saka is close: Saka benefits from Arsenal’s fixtures and Gameweek 10 captaincy against Hull, but Palmer’s lack of European football should make his long-term minutes more secure.

The defensive core remains intact. Triple Arsenal defence is still backed despite a recent concession, with David Raya, Riccardo Calafiori and the other Arsenal defenders retaining substantial clean-sheet upside against Leeds. Lewis Hall is fine to keep and play for Coventry, thanks to attacking threat and set pieces, but is less compelling as a new purchase given Newcastle’s defensive fragility and a tougher medium-term run. Liverpool defenders are holds rather than buys before Manchester City, Brentford and Arsenal. Managers are urged not to chase one-week swings, force transfers because of a disappointing wildcard, or overreact to early ranks in a season with 33 gameweeks remaining.
key_points: Sangare is the leading Gameweek 6 sale because uncertain starts and reduced minutes severely limit his defensive-contribution upside.
Sharda is a strong longer-term midfield target, while Josh King and Pascal Gross are other attractive budget options.
Szoboszlai can be sold, but Sangare should generally be moved first unless selling Szoboszlai unlocks a clearly superior move.
Do not make early transfers during the international break unless protecting a decisive price change; injuries and team news can alter the plan.
Keep Yoane Wissa for Coventry despite his missed penalty, as he remains on penalties and was unlucky not to return.
If Joao Pedro is ruled out for Gameweek 6, Gonzalo Garcia is a credible replacement; if Pedro is fit, rolling a transfer is viable.
Palmer is the current captain, with Haaland, Bruno Fernandes and Saka all legitimate alternatives depending on transfers and international minutes.
Triple Arsenal defence remains a viable hold for Leeds at home, while Lewis Hall is a keep rather than an obvious new buy.

items.headline: Haaland and Arsenal’s defence anchor a provisional Gameweek 6 Wildcard
items.summary:
The Gameweek 6 plan is overwhelmingly likely to be a Wildcard, although it is not formally activated yet. A series of early transfers has created a nominal -32, but those hits disappear once either the Wildcard or Free Hit is played. Keeping the chip unconfirmed preserves a remote Free Hit escape route should multiple intended targets pick up international-break injuries, while also allowing moves to capture potential price rises.

Erling Haaland is locked into the draft despite a quiet Gameweek 5 captaincy return, with Manchester City projected among the strongest attacks over the next five gameweeks. Arsenal are the other major commitment: David Raya, Riccardo Calafiori and Ezri Konsa are currently set to form a defensive triple-up. The view is that Arsenal remain comfortably the league’s best defence, while Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard can be matched by cheaper midfield alternatives. Raya is the least certain Arsenal selection; a cheaper rotating goalkeeper pair, potentially including James Trafford, is an alternative if the third Arsenal slot is needed elsewhere.

Defensive depth is a key Wildcard objective after a poor start to the season for bench coverage. Rather than carrying a £4.0m non-playing defender, the squad is built around five usable defenders and a rotation featuring Arsenal, Brighton, Tottenham and Leeds assets. Jan Paul van Hecke appeals for defensive-contribution points and set-piece threat, while Spurs and Leeds defenders are selected more for their fixture rotation than absolute clean-sheet security. Djed Spence, Luka Vuskovic, James Justin and Jayden Bogle remain under consideration as cheaper alternatives.

Midfield is the biggest unresolved area. Pascal Gross is considered essential, while Harvey Barnes is favoured over Anthony Elanga/other Newcastle alternatives because he looks secure for minutes, has decent fixtures and avoids European rotation. Morgan Gibbs-White offers penalties, talisman status and no European schedule, but Nottingham Forest’s difficult run makes him vulnerable to replacement by Antoine Semenyo, Rayan Cherki or another higher-upside pick. Cole Palmer versus Morgan Rogers is another major budget decision, with Palmer’s premium Chelsea upside weighed against Rogers freeing funds for improvements elsewhere. Joao Pedro stays up front if his injury prognosis permits, even if he misses Gameweek 6, because Kevin Schade can cover from the bench; Yoane Wissa and Fulham’s Gonzalo are competing alternatives, with Fulham’s strong five-match run particularly attractive.

The final Wildcard will be shaped by international-break fitness news, price changes and the need to differentiate from managers who Wildcarded in Gameweeks 3 and 4. Barnes and Schade are seen as lower-owned, no-Europe options who could provide that differentiation, whereas the uncertain spots remain the second Chelsea attacker, Gibbs-White’s replacement, the third forward and the goalkeeper structure.
key_points: The Gameweek 6 Wildcard is nearly certain, but remains unactivated so a Free Hit can still be used if international-break injuries wreck the planned squad.
Erling Haaland is a firm inclusion, with Manchester City rated among the best attacks for Gameweeks 6-10.
A triple Arsenal defence of David Raya, Riccardo Calafiori and Ezri Konsa is the current plan, although Raya could become a rotating goalkeeper combination.
Five playable defenders are preferred over a £4.0m bench option, using Arsenal, Brighton, Spurs and Leeds assets to rotate fixtures.
Pascal Gross is viewed as a permanent midfield pick, while Harvey Barnes is strongly favoured for secure minutes, fixtures and freedom from European competition.
Morgan Gibbs-White is under pressure from Semenyo or Cherki because Nottingham Forest have a poor fixture run despite Gibbs-White’s penalties and talisman role.
Cole Palmer versus Morgan Rogers is a major Wildcard budget call, with Rogers offering funds for upgrades elsewhere.
Joao Pedro remains in the forward draft if his injury is short term, with Kevin Schade able to cover, while Wissa and Fulham’s Gonzalo are alternatives.

items.headline: Haaland remains Gameweek 5 captain as João Pedro injury tests FPL managers’ patience
items.summary:
Erling Haaland is the standout Gameweek 5 captain at home to Sunderland, with Manchester City expected to be fresh after rotating in midweek. Morgan Gibbs-White, at home to Coventry, is the leading differential alternative and arguably the second-best captain, but Haaland’s superior projected output makes him the safer call. Triple-captaining Haaland is viable this week, although Fulham at home in Gameweek 11, Hull at home later in the season and Ipswich at home also loom as potential opportunities.

João Pedro is not expected to start after reports of a knee-ligament issue requiring around three-and-a-half weeks of recovery. That makes him likely to miss Gameweek 5 and leaves some doubt over his availability after the international break. Despite that, the recommended approach for managers with a playable bench and only limited free transfers is to hold João Pedro, accept an auto-sub and carry transfers into the unusually long break. Selling him now for a short-term replacement may require another transfer to buy him back, particularly as Brighton remain top of the league for expected goals and have a favourable home match against Bournemouth after the break.

For managers who are wildcarding in Gameweek 6, or who cannot field 11 players, selling João Pedro is much easier to justify. Thierno Barry, at home to Ipswich, is the preferred replacement due to his strong early expected-goal numbers and another appealing fixture against Hull to follow. Dominic Calvert-Lewin is also attractive against a depleted Crystal Palace side, while Yoane Wissa and Liam Delap are viable one-week alternatives. Gibbs-White is the premium midfield punt of the week, and a move such as João Pedro and a weak midfielder to Barry and Gibbs-White has major short-term upside for managers planning an imminent wildcard.

Ben White is also a transfer concern after Thomas Tuchel indicates that he is injured and likely absent from the England squad. Nottingham Forest defenders, especially Nico Williams, Murillo and potentially Neco Williams, offer attacking or clean-sheet upside for the Coventry fixture; Daniel Muñoz is another aggressive one-week replacement. Avoid unnecessary hits for defenders unless they are needed to field a full side. Free Hit is best reserved for teams carrying several injuries and poor fixtures, but it is a credible Gameweek 5 play for squads containing João Pedro, Brighton assets against Arsenal, suspended or injured Manchester City players and other unavailable starters.
key_points: Captain Haaland against Sunderland; Gibbs-White is the best differential vice-captain option for Coventry at home.
João Pedro is not expected to start in Gameweek 5 after reported knee-ligament damage, with a possible return around Gameweek 6.
Hold João Pedro if you have cover and are not wildcarding soon, as selling and rebuying him likely costs two transfers.
Barry is the preferred João Pedro replacement for wildcarders or managers needing an immediate starter, with Ipswich and Hull next.
Calvert-Lewin is a strong one-week punt against injury-hit Crystal Palace, but Arsenal in Gameweek 6 makes bench cover important.
Ben White is a likely absentee; consider Forest defenders such as Nico Williams or Murillo, or Daniel Muñoz for upside.
Avoid defender hits where possible, and use Free Hit only if injuries and poor fixtures leave your squad badly compromised.
Gibbs-White is the leading midfield transfer target, while Harvey Barnes and Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall are cheaper upside options.

items.headline: Haaland remains the clear Gameweek 5 captain as João Pedro absence triggers FPL panic
items.summary:
Erling Haaland is the standout Gameweek 5 captain, with Manchester City projected for roughly 2.4 goals and Haaland expected to dominate their goal involvement. Morgan Gibbs-White is a strong Nottingham Forest option and a viable vice-captain, but he is not viewed as a reason to take an early-season captaincy gamble or use the Triple Captain chip. Calvert-Lewin and Barry are attractive forward plays, while Newcastle assets are less convincing than the market projections suggest: Hull are expected to sit deep and Newcastle have created very few chances so far.

João Pedro is absent from Chelsea’s squad for the Brentford match after withdrawing from Brazil duty with knee swelling. The expectation is that he misses Gameweek 5 but returns after the international break for Gameweek 6, with Bournemouth at home and Everton away making him worth retaining. Managers are advised to bench him rather than sell, especially if moving him out would require two transfers, sacrifice team value or create no route back to a severely underpriced Chelsea forward. Starting Pedro before confirmed team news is reasonable only because the likely outcomes are a start or no appearance; once his non-start is confirmed, he belongs on the bench to avoid a one-point cameo risk.

The central recommendation is to stay calm rather than chase a perfect XI. A João Pedro absence for one week should not force a hit, a double transfer or a Free Hit if the squad still contains playable cover such as Conor, Gross, Thomas, Sangaré, Solly March, Egan or similar budget options. Gross is the preferred Pedro replacement from the bench in many squads, although Arsenal’s defence is still backed over Brighton attackers. Sangaré loses appeal after being named on Brentford’s bench, increasing the risk of a late one-point substitute appearance.

Free Hit use is generally discouraged this week because the upside is limited for teams that already own Haaland, Arsenal defenders, Newcastle coverage or Leeds/Everton forwards. A Free Hit should ideally target a week with several elite sides facing weak opposition, rather than being used to add extra Everton, Newcastle or Forest players. For those already committed to the chip, a high-upside draft centres on Haaland, Calvert-Lewin, Barry, Gibbs-White, Bukayo Saka, Antoine Semenyo, Rayan Cherki, Daniel Muñoz, Neco Williams, Lewis Hall and Manchester City defensive coverage. Wildcard managers can build around Raya, Calafiori, Conor, Hall, Palmer, Gibbs-White, Saka, Rogers, João Pedro, Haaland and Barry, while keeping enough playable depth to cover Pedro temporarily.

Liverpool attackers are not a priority buy despite Bournemouth, with concerns over Liverpool’s attacking rhythm and rotation once Barcelona signing Barcola is fully integrated. Ben White is also a sell candidate after England’s injury information contradicts Arsenal’s vague availability comments. The broader strategy entering the international break is to preserve transfers, accept imperfect fixtures and avoid reactive moves that leave squads exposed to injuries or price changes over the break.
key_points: Captain Haaland in Gameweek 5; Gibbs-White is a strong vice-captain but not a preferred captain or Triple Captain alternative.
João Pedro is not in Chelsea’s squad for Brentford, but is expected back around Gameweek 6, so bench and hold rather than sell in most squads.
Avoid taking a minus four to replace João Pedro, particularly if it leaves no easy route to buy him back after the international break.
Do not Free Hit merely to replace Pedro or chase Forest, Everton and Newcastle assets; the likely gain is too small for most teams.
Start playable cover such as Conor, Gross, Thomas, Egan or Solly March rather than forcing a transfer; Gross is a reasonable first substitute despite the Arsenal fixture.
Sangaré is on Brentford’s bench, making him a risky João Pedro replacement because of the possibility of a one-point cameo.
Ben White is an increasingly obvious sell if a transfer is needed, with injury reports suggesting he is unlikely to start.
Liverpool attackers, including Gakpo, are not priority transfers in due to rotation concerns and doubts over Liverpool’s current attacking fluency.

items.headline: João Pedro Absence Pushes FPL Managers Towards Bench Cover, Not a Panic Sale
items.summary:
João Pedro is expected to miss Chelsea’s Gameweek 5 match after withdrawing from the Brazil squad and being omitted from the matchday squad, but the recommendation is to keep him for most managers. He is likely to return around Gameweek 6, so selling him before a three-week international break risks needing another transfer to buy him back at a higher price. Managers who have already used their Wildcard should start Pedro if possible, place a strong substitute first on the bench and avoid making non-essential moves before the break.

The exception is for managers committed to a Gameweek 6 Wildcard. With the Wildcard able to erase short-term hits and rebuild the squad after the break, a one-week punt becomes viable. The preferred move is Ola Aina to Neco Williams, with Nottingham Forest hosting Coventry. Williams is playing as a wing-back, carries attacking upside and faces a Coventry side that concedes heavily down its left flank. Daniel Muñoz is favoured if affordable, while Everton’s Thierno Barry, Brentford’s Yoane Wissa and Liam Delap are alternative short-term Pedro replacements, though Barry is viewed as a less convincing long-term pick despite Ipswich at home.

Erling Haaland is the clear captain for Gameweek 5 against Sunderland, with Morgan Gibbs-White a viable vice-captain rather than a preferred armband alternative. Triple-captaining Haaland is not advised: Sunderland are not viewed as a side likely to concede a huge score, even if City remain strong favourites. Pascal Groß is backed as a useful Pedro replacement from the bench and is generally preferred to Arsenal defenders such as Ezri Konsa or Jurrien Timber in close selection calls, despite Brighton facing Arsenal.

A Gameweek 6 Wildcard remains the intended strategy for a squad containing players such as Dominik Szoboszlai, Antoine Semenyo, Dominic Calvert-Lewin, Leeds defenders and limited defensive rotation. The issue is less one disastrous player than repeated weak starts across the coming weeks, including difficult fixtures for Leeds, Liverpool and Calvert-Lewin. The planned Wildcard prioritises Arsenal, Brighton, Leeds and Tottenham defensive rotation, with Raya, Gabriel/Calafiori, Groß, Gibbs-White and João Pedro among the key considerations. During the break, early transfers are used selectively to capture price rises, but the Wildcard is not activated immediately in case the Free Hit becomes preferable.
key_points: João Pedro is not in Chelsea’s Gameweek 5 squad, but managers who have already used their Wildcard should generally hold him and use bench cover.
Managers set on a Gameweek 6 Wildcard can sell Pedro for a one-week punt, with Neco Williams the preferred transfer for Nottingham Forest versus Coventry.
Daniel Muñoz is an appealing alternative if affordable, while Wissa, Barry and Delap are short-term forward options rather than clear long-term solutions.
Haaland is the recommended Gameweek 5 captain against Sunderland; Gibbs-White is a strong vice-captain, but Triple Captain is not advised.
Pascal Groß is a credible first substitute for Pedro and is preferred over several marginal defensive starts despite Brighton facing Arsenal.
The Gameweek 6 Wildcard is aimed at improving squad depth and fixture rotation rather than solving one emergency, with Arsenal-Brighton-Leeds-Spurs defensive coverage under consideration.
Avoid hits to remove Pedro unless a manager lacks enough starters; the three-week break makes a transfer out-and-back especially inefficient.
Price-rise chasing during the break can add squad value, but the Wildcard should be delayed until closer to Gameweek 6 to preserve Free Hit flexibility.

items.headline: João Pedro doubt leaves FPL managers weighing a roll against Barry and Gibbs-White punts
items.summary:
João Pedro is expected to miss Gameweek 5 after withdrawing from the Brazil squad, although Chelsea do not formally rule him out before the deadline. The key uncertainty is whether the knee issue also keeps him out of Gameweek 6 after the international break. That makes him sellable, particularly for managers with a weak bench or a Wildcard planned soon, but holding remains viable if a playable substitute such as Ezri Konsa, Pascal Groß or Nico Williams can cover him.

The most attractive short-term replacements are Thierno Barry at home to Ipswich and Morgan Gibbs-White at home to Coventry. Barry offers a cheap route out of João Pedro and preserves funds, while Gibbs-White combines a favourable fixture with penalties and strong bonus-point potential. A two-transfer move from João Pedro and Sangaré to Barry and Gibbs-White is repeatedly described as reasonable, especially for managers with three free transfers or a Gameweek 6 Wildcard. However, there is a clear downside: using both transfers before an international break leaves less flexibility to react to injuries and rotation news.

The preferred approach for a team with two free transfers, a decent bench and no pressing structural issues is to roll, even if it means accepting João Pedro’s likely absence. Banking transfers is particularly valuable ahead of the break, and a strong squad can absorb one missing forward. The argument against rolling is that Barry versus Ipswich and Gibbs-White versus Coventry are two of the best immediate fixtures available, while João Pedro may remain unavailable next week. Ultimately, both routes are defensible, but the final decision is to hold João Pedro, start him for the automatic substitution, and carry three free transfers into Gameweek 6.

Erling Haaland is the standout captain for Gameweek 5 against Sunderland. Triple-captaining him is not considered essential, but it is a viable aggressive play because he has had a full week off and is expected to start. Alternatives such as Gibbs-White, Bruno Fernandes, Beto and Dominic Calvert-Lewin are discussed, but none is preferred over Haaland. Managers should not overreact to Haaland’s record of two scoreless matches against Sunderland.

For defenders, the analysis favours Lewis Hall for the next two fixtures, while Nikola Milenković and Neco Williams are strong Forest options, with Daniel Muñoz the more expensive attacking pick. Arsenal defenders remain good season-long assets but are less appealing on a Gameweek 5 Free Hit because Brighton are capable of scoring. Free Hitting into a Gameweek 6 Wildcard is generally discouraged: a Wildcard now is preferable for squads carrying several genuine problems, while teams with only João Pedro and one or two doubts should save the chips.
key_points: João Pedro is highly unlikely to feature in Gameweek 5, and his possible absence in Gameweek 6 is the main reason to consider selling him.
Barry at home to Ipswich is the preferred cheap one-week or short-term João Pedro replacement, while Gonzalo García is also liked over the next several fixtures.
Gibbs-White is a strong Gameweek 5 target against Coventry, with penalties and bonus potential adding to his appeal.
João Pedro and Sangaré to Barry and Gibbs-White is a viable two-transfer move, but rolling is preferred when it would otherwise leave only one free transfer through the international break.
Haaland is the top captain against Sunderland; Triple Captain is acceptable but not clearly superior to waiting for later fixtures such as Hull at home in Gameweek 16.
Managers with a serviceable bench should start João Pedro and allow an automatic substitute such as Konsa or Groß to replace him rather than forcing a hit.
Lewis Hall is preferred for immediate fixtures, while Milenković, Williams and Muñoz are attractive Forest defensive options.
Avoid Free Hitting purely to cover João Pedro, especially if planning to Wildcard in Gameweek 6; the returning squad may still contain the same problems.

items.title: CHELSEA LATEST ⚠️ | FPL GW5 INJURY + TEAM NEWS 🚨|  FPL Tips 2026/27
items.headline: Joao Pedro expected to miss Gameweek 5 as Chelsea injury information comes under scrutiny
items.summary:
Joao Pedro is the major Fantasy Premier League concern ahead of Gameweek 5. Chelsea do not definitively rule him out against Brentford, but his omission from Brazil’s squad and reports of knee oedema with a recovery estimate of around three and a half weeks make an immediate appearance highly unlikely. He is viewed as a realistic Gameweek 6 doubt rather than a long-term sell, with a likely return by Gameweek 7, so managers with playable bench cover are advised to hold rather than spend two transfers or use a chip. Danny Welbeck is the likeliest replacement up front.

The uncertainty around Pedro is part of a wider warning over Chelsea and Arsenal team news. Reece James is also absent from the England squad through injury despite Chelsea’s guarded update, while Ben White is reportedly injured after Arsenal initially suggested their group was in good shape. William Saliba is definitely sidelined for a prolonged spell; Cristhian Mosquera and Piero Hincapie are also doubts, while Jurrien Timber is more likely to be available but may not be certain to start.

There are several useful returnees and selection clues elsewhere. Tottenham expect Pedro Porro and Sandro Tonali back, Aston Villa should have Emiliano Martinez available, and Ismaila Sarr returns for Crystal Palace but may be limited if he starts. Manchester City could have Jeremy Doku back from injury, probably initially from the bench, while Phil Foden serves a three-match suspension. City’s midweek rotation points towards a fresher league XI, with Rayan Cherki’s half-time withdrawal making him a stronger candidate to start against Sunderland.

Newcastle’s injury list makes their assets and opposition selections harder to judge: Anthony Elanga faces a potentially lengthy absence pending a scan, while Derrick, Jacob Ramsey and Douglas Luiz are also ruled out. Crystal Palace remain without Dean Henderson and Jean-Philippe Mateta, with Mateta potentially absent beyond Gameweek 5, while Disasi begins a three-match ban. Managers considering defensive cover should also note that Hull are without N'Golo Kante through concussion protocol, while Coventry lose centre-back Amenda and striker Taiwo Awoniyi is suspended.
key_points: Hold Joao Pedro if bench cover is available: he is expected to miss Brentford but may return in Gameweek 6 or, more likely, Gameweek 7.

items.title: JOAO PEDRO INJURED! 🚨🇧🇷 SELL OR KEEP? 📱 MY FPL GW5 TEAM SELECTION! #fpl  #premierleague  #chelsea
items.headline: João Pedro exit pushes Everton’s Barry to the front of Gameweek 5 transfer plans
items.summary:
João Pedro’s withdrawal from the Brazil squad creates the key selection issue ahead of Gameweek 5, with his availability for Brentford now considered very unlikely. With a Gameweek 6 wildcard already planned, selling the forward for a one-week punt is viewed as a flexible move despite the value lost, because he can be bought back immediately on the wildcard.

The leading replacement is Everton’s Barry, who hosts Ipswich, a side judged to have been particularly poor defensively this season. Newcastle’s Wissa and Delap, who faces Coventry, are alternative forward options, but Barry is the likeliest move. Another route is selling Ayew for Nottingham Forest’s Williams and switching to a back four, with Williams having Coventry at home, although the João Pedro move takes priority.

Kinski starts in goal at home to Aston Villa ahead of Verbruggen. The defence is expected to include Harry Maguire away to Fulham, Muharemovic at home to Crystal Palace and Calafiori away to Brighton; Maguire’s fixture is not ideal, but he is preferred to Diop and Ayew. A defensive transfer had been considered, while Szoboszlai’s disappointing form also makes him a possible concern, but both issues are deferred because the forward line needs attention before the wildcard.

In midfield, Brennan Johnson, Cole Palmer and the recently purchased Gibbs-White are selected, with Gibbs-White’s home fixture against Coventry particularly appealing. Haaland leads the attack and receives the captaincy armband at home to Sunderland, while Gibbs-White becomes vice-captain following the João Pedro injury concern. The planned Barry transfer is not yet confirmed, leaving room to react before the deadline.
key_points: Sell João Pedro before the Gameweek 6 wildcard if his Brazil withdrawal rules him out against Brentford, accepting a short-term loss of team value.
Everton’s Barry, at home to Ipswich, is the preferred one-week forward punt because Ipswich have looked weak defensively.
Wissa of Newcastle and Delap against Coventry are the main alternative replacements for João Pedro.
Haaland is captain at home to Sunderland, with Gibbs-White vice-captain for his home match against Coventry.
Kinski starts over Verbruggen in goal despite facing Aston Villa.
A defensive transfer and a potential Szoboszlai exit are postponed, with the João Pedro situation taking priority.

items.title: FPL GW5 Final Thoughts 🔥 João Pedro update 🚨 Benching Headaches 🤕
items.headline: Hold Joao Pedro despite Gameweek 5 absence as Haaland leads captaincy plans
items.summary:
Joao Pedro is expected to miss Chelsea’s Gameweek 5 trip to Brentford despite not being formally ruled out by Enzo Maresca. Reports from Brazil suggest a knee issue involving swelling around the ACL and MCL, with a recovery period of roughly three and a half weeks; that points to rest through the international break and a likely Gameweek 6 return. There is a small risk he also misses Gameweek 6 or returns with managed minutes, but the recommended default is to keep him, start him if necessary and rely on a functioning bench rather than spend transfers removing a player likely to be wanted again soon.

The exception is a Wildcard: Joao Pedro is not an appealing inclusion when he is certain or highly likely to miss Gameweek 5 and not fully certain for Gameweek 6. Managers can instead take a short-term forward punt such as Evanilson/Barry against Ipswich, Wissa against Hull, Calvert-Lewin against Crystal Palace or possibly Liam Delap, while retaining enough money to buy Joao Pedro back. Danny Welbeck is not favoured as a one-week replacement, because Chelsea’s Brentford fixture is less attractive than the alternatives and several rival forwards may have penalty duties.

Manchester City’s Sunderland home match is a major target. Erling Haaland is the standout captain after a full midweek rest, while Josko Gvardiol and Ruben Dias look strong clean-sheet options after also being rested. Rayan Cherki plays only 45 minutes in the cup and is still expected to start in the No. 10 role, so he is worth holding; O’Reilly, by contrast, is considered a sell or bench risk, with Gvardiol expected at left-back. Enzo Fernandez is highlighted as a potentially excellent City midfield asset if Elliot Anderson provides the deeper defensive cover, while Antoine Semenyo is expected to occupy one wide role.

Morgan Gibbs-White remains the desired transfer target for Nottingham Forest’s home game against Coventry, with Daniel Munoz preferred to Neco Williams when budget allows because of his greater attacking upside. However, the presented squad is likely to roll two free transfers rather than sell Joao Pedro and Sosa/Szoboszlai for Barry and Gibbs-White before the international break. That aggressive double move offers differential upside, but creates a later problem of buying Joao Pedro back and leaves less flexibility for injuries. A Gameweek 5 Free Hit is viable for squads carrying several short-term issues, but is not recommended solely for Joao Pedro; Gameweeks 12 or 16 are preferred potential Free Hit windows due to difficult City-Arsenal fixtures and stronger opportunities to target multiple less-owned teams.
key_points: Captain Erling Haaland in Gameweek 5, with Manchester City at home to Sunderland and Haaland fully rested in the cup.
Hold Joao Pedro in most non-Wildcard squads, expect him to miss Gameweek 5, and use bench cover with a view to a probable Gameweek 6 return.
Avoid Joao Pedro on a Gameweek 5 Wildcard unless accepting the fitness uncertainty; short-term alternatives include Barry/Evanilson, Wissa and Calvert-Lewin.
Keep Rayan Cherki after his 45-minute cup outing, but treat O’Reilly as a likely non-starter and a potential transfer out before Sunderland.
Target Manchester City defenders Gvardiol and Ruben Dias for a clean sheet, with Gvardiol offering the higher attacking ceiling.
Morgan Gibbs-White and Daniel Munoz are premium Nottingham Forest targets against Coventry, while Neco Williams is the cheaper defensive alternative.
Newcastle’s Dan Burn, Ramsey, Alanga and Dedic are ruled out for Gameweek 5; Livramento is expected to cover if fit, while Hull’s Mendy misses out with concussion.
Do not force a one-week transfer before a Gameweek 6 Wildcard, as free transfers roll through Wildcards and Free Hits.

items.title: FPL GW5 Team Selection: João Pedro is INJURED! ⚠️ What To Do? | Transfers & Captain
items.headline: João Pedro injury prompts patience as Haaland remains Gameweek 5 captain
items.summary:
Dan enters Gameweek 5 at around 15,000th overall after a 93-point Gameweek 4, with every starter returning and his wildcard squad providing the depth needed to absorb João Pedro’s likely absence. His main plan is not to sell the Chelsea forward: reports from ESPN Brazil suggest a knee sprain-related issue keeps João Pedro out for roughly three and a half weeks, making him unlikely for Gameweek 5 but potentially available again after the long international break in Gameweek 6.

Rather than spend transfers on a short-term replacement, he starts João Pedro and relies on Ezri Konsa’s automatic substitution if the forward misses out. The logic is that João Pedro is still an elite-value asset whom managers will soon want back, while selling and rebuying him risks wasting transfers and losing value. Pascal Groß is also available as cover in Gameweek 6 if the recovery takes longer than expected. Managers without dependable bench cover can consider Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who rotates well with Groß, or Gonzalo as a short-term option, but should only sell João Pedro if necessary.

Erling Haaland is the clear captain against Sunderland after being rested in midweek, with Bukayo Saka the preferred vice-captain against Brighton. Brighton lead the league for attacking underlying numbers, including shots in the box and big chances, so Dan avoids relying on a double or triple Arsenal defensive return despite Saka’s strong attacking potential. He benches Konsa away to Brighton, starts Riccardo Calafiori for his attacking upside, and backs Kinsky at home to Aston Villa, whose underlying attacking figures are among the league’s weakest. Lewis Hall is also favoured against Hull, while Mermović starts at home to Crystal Palace.

In midfield, he keeps Dominik Szoboszlai despite mounting interest in Morgan Gibbs-White. Gibbs-White has the better fixtures, so a straightforward one-transfer switch is reasonable, but Dan argues that their underlying output is broadly similar to Groß’s and that recent points differences are largely variance. Szoboszlai takes more shots and creates more chances than Gibbs-White, has set-piece routes to returns against a Bournemouth side vulnerable to dead balls, and could benefit if Liverpool move him into a more advanced role. With two free transfers and a deep squad, the priority is to preserve flexibility through the international break rather than force moves for fixture appeal alone.
key_points: Captain Erling Haaland against Sunderland in Gameweek 5, with Bukayo Saka the preferred vice-captain against Brighton.
João Pedro is expected to miss Gameweek 5 with a reported knee-ligament sprain issue but may return in Gameweek 6 after the extended international break.
Keep João Pedro if possible: start him in case he is unexpectedly fit and use a reliable bench player such as Ezri Konsa as the automatic substitute.
Selling João Pedro for a one-week replacement is discouraged because he remains strong value and may require an immediate buy-back.
Dominic Calvert-Lewin is a plausible João Pedro replacement for managers who must sell, particularly because he rotates well with Pascal Groß; Gonzalo is another short-term consideration.
Bench Konsa against Brighton because Brighton lead the league in xG, shots in the box and big chances, making Arsenal defensive investment less appealing this week.
Start Kinsky against Aston Villa, whose attack ranks among the weakest by xG, and back Lewis Hall for clean-sheet and set-piece upside against Hull.

Do not force Szoboszlai to Morgan Gibbs-White for multiple transfers: Gibbs-White’s fixtures are better, but the players’ underlying numbers are close and Szoboszlai retains set-piece upside against Bournemouth.

items.title: KEEP JOAO PEDRO? 🤔 | THE FPL Q&A GW5 WITH TOM + SAM! ⁉️ | FPL Tips 26/27
items.headline: João Pedro injury prompts bench-and-hold call as Calvert-Lewin challenges Haaland captaincy
items.summary:
João Pedro is expected to miss Gameweek 5 after withdrawing from the Brazil squad and failing to appear in Brighton training material, with a Friday-night match against Brentford likely to confirm his absence. However, the recommendation is generally to hold rather than sell: managers who bought him at £7.5m lose value by cashing out at £7.8m, and a one-game absence either side of the international break is not worth a transfer if a playable bench option is available. Selling for Liam Delap or Newcastle’s Yoane Wissa is viewed as too speculative, while a short-term switch to Dominic Calvert-Lewin is the preferred replacement only for managers who are wildcarding next week or otherwise need to move Pedro on.

Erling Haaland remains the safe captain for Gameweek 5 at home despite strong alternatives. Calvert-Lewin is the standout differential captaincy candidate, while Morgan Gibbs-White also has major appeal against Coventry, but Haaland’s ownership and home fixture make him difficult to oppose in a week without an obvious premium rival. Gibbs-White is already a useful differential simply by being owned, so there is less need to compound that risk with the armband. A Triple Captain on Gibbs-White is a viable high-risk punt rather than a recommendation.

Nottingham Forest are the favoured source of transfers. Neco Williams ranks above Malick Thiaw and Jarrad Branthwaite as a Rodon replacement because of his clean-sheet prospects, attacking potential and longer-term value. Gibbs-White is worth buying over Xavi Simons or Dominik Szoboszlai in some cases, even with only one free transfer, thanks to fixtures against Coventry and Crystal Palace; Forest midfielder Elliot Anderson is highlighted as a cheaper differential, with improved attacking involvement under Oliver Glasner. Morgan Rogers, by contrast, is a clear hold and should not be sacrificed for Gibbs-White.

Newcastle’s fixture run, beginning with Hull at home, looks appealing on paper but does not yet justify defensive investment after a 4-1 defeat and several injuries, including Anthony Elanga, Dan Burn, Jacob Ramsey and Nico Gonzalez. Wissa is the only Newcastle consideration, but Hull have impressed and could score, so Calvert-Lewin should not be sold for him this week. Brighton’s Kaoru Mitoma remains usable despite a difficult run because he is currently first choice on the left and retains attacking upside, although he is better benched against Arsenal if possible. Managers planning a Gameweek 6 wildcard are encouraged to consider a core of Haaland, João Pedro if fit, budget midfielders such as Rogers, and Arsenal coverage led by Bukayo Saka rather than Cole Palmer or a triple Chelsea attack.
key_points: Hold João Pedro if you have credible bench cover, as his expected Gameweek 5 absence may only be short-term and selling sacrifices accumulated price value.
Captain Haaland in Gameweek 5; Calvert-Lewin is the leading differential armband option and Gibbs-White is another high-upside alternative.
Neco Williams is the preferred budget defensive transfer over Malick Thiaw and Jarrad Branthwaite, with Forest’s fixture run and his attacking threat both attractive.
Gibbs-White is a strong buy for Coventry and Crystal Palace, while Elliot Anderson offers a cheaper Forest midfield differential.
Do not sell Morgan Rogers for Gibbs-White, as Rogers remains secure for minutes and continues to return.
Avoid rushing into Newcastle defenders despite their favourable fixtures; Wissa is a watchlist option rather than an immediate priority.
For João Pedro replacements, Calvert-Lewin is best for a one-week punt before a wildcard, while Garcia is preferred for a longer-term move.
A Gameweek 6 wildcard structure can favour Saka, João Pedro if fit, Rogers and Haaland, with Palmer not considered essential.

items.title: FPL GW5 BEST PLAYERS TO BUY! 💰🎯 #fpl  #premierleague  #football
items.headline: Target Everton’s Ipswich fixture as Barry, Branthwaite and Dewsbury-Hall lead GW5 buys
items.summary:
Everton are the standout Gameweek 5 target because Ipswich visit Goodison Park before a favourable longer-term run. Thierno Barry is the leading forward pick: he ranks second in the league for expected goals after four gameweeks, behind only Erling Haaland, and offers both immediate upside and a route into Everton’s improving fixtures. In defence, Jarrad Branthwaite is the preferred option, with James Tarkowski available for more money and Vitalii Mykolenko as the cheaper alternative. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall is also attractive at £6.5m, offering a similar all-round midfield profile to Morgan Gibbs-White at a lower price.

Newcastle’s recent defensive returns have disappointed, but their fixture run still makes Malick Thiaw and Lewis Hall viable defensive investments. Yoane Wissa is the more long-term Newcastle attacking buy; his last couple of matches are underwhelming, but the schedule is strong enough to justify patience. Managers should prioritise players who are secure starters and can benefit from this fixture swing rather than chasing short-term form alone.

Nottingham Forest provide another useful entry point, led by Morgan Gibbs-White in midfield ahead of Coventry at home and Crystal Palace away. Neco Williams is the preferred Forest defender over the slightly pricier Lucas Digne, while Brentford’s Vitaly Janelt is a budget midfield differential at £5.0m: he has played 90 minutes in every match, reached DefCon in three of four games and produced attacking returns twice. Arsenal remain the safest defensive investment for managers without a triple-up, even with Brighton away in Gameweek 5; Riccardo Calafiori is among the key options. Brighton themselves are best avoided despite a strong opening four weeks, as they sit bottom of the fixture ticker across the next five matches.
key_points: Thierno Barry is the priority forward buy for Gameweek 5 after ranking second for expected goals, with Ipswich at home offering an immediate fixture boost.
Jarrad Branthwaite is the preferred Everton defender; Tarkowski costs more, while Mykolenko is the budget route into the same defence.
Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall is a £6.5m alternative to Morgan Gibbs-White with Everton’s strong upcoming schedule.
Yoane Wissa is a longer-term Newcastle pick despite recent blanks, because Newcastle’s fixture run remains difficult to ignore.
Morgan Gibbs-White and Neco Williams are strong Nottingham Forest targets ahead of Coventry at home and Crystal Palace away.
Vitaly Janelt is a £5.0m Brentford differential with reliable minutes, three DefCon scores and returns in two of four matches.
Arsenal defenders, including Riccardo Calafiori, remain a safe investment for managers without three Arsenal players, while Brighton are a short-term avoid due to their poor upcoming fixtures.
